headline: Medium risk: shared project-directory writes can leak or corrupt outputs; no direct prompt-injection or compliance pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and can later run generated code, while pathway has no filesystem access or output channel. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff through shared project artifacts, so direct injection is limited and not default. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF operator copies gpt-engineer-generated text into pathway prompts, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF pathway is configured to ingest project files from the same directory, then file-based instruction smuggling becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Review any text copied from agent A before feeding it to agent B.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted project files in pathway.
Use a human approval step before executing A's generated code.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the user project directory and may handle OPENAI_API_KEY, while pathway has no filesystem or network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage is mainly via manual placement of sensitive files into A's project directory, not an automatic cross-agent channel.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the project directory used by gpt-engineer, then A can read them.
IF pathway is later pointed at the same directory through external orchestration, then copied data could be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the project directory.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Redact sensitive files before running gpt-engineer.
Verify pathway inputs do not include A's generated artifacts unless intended.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad filesystem write and per-project shared state via the project directory; pathway is a document-processing agent with no write capability, so direct write-write conflict is absent. However, if an orchestrator feeds both the same mutable directory, A can overwrite artifacts that B later consumes, creating a default-unsafe coordination risk that is not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory, then A can overwrite files that B reads or transforms.
IF an external orchestrator lacks locking, then concurrent edits can race on shared artifacts.
mitigations: Add file locks in the orchestrator.
Serialize runs so only one agent mutates shared artifacts at a time.
Snapshot the workspace before handing it from A to B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code and write files, and pathway can process documents, so a common workflow could pass A's outputs into B without verification. Because pathway has no documented critical-evaluation or action-taking safeguards in the profile, the pair can propagate incorrect code or instructions into downstream work products, though not into irreversible actions by itself.
conditions: IF pathway ingests gpt-engineer output as authoritative input, then A's mistakes can cascade into B's outputs.
IF B is used to transform A-generated code or docs without review, then errors can be amplified across work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require schema or lint validation on A's outputs before B consumes them.
Keep provenance metadata on files passed from A to B.
Reject unverified claims or code blocks from A unless checked.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: gpt-engineer is open-source, handles generated source code and an API key, and pathway's profile lists no data classes, residency, or retention obligations. Without a documented regulated data class or residency mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, then a separate compliance review is required.
IF pathway is configured with a retention or residency policy not shown in the profile, then reassess compliance.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review residency and retention settings if they are later enabled.
